root_cause.text: The `mm_drop_cid_on_cpu()` function in the scheduler MMCID subsystem failed to validate that the CID was actually CPU-owned before manipulating its state, causing out-of-bounds access when the `TRANSIT` flag was set

relevance_review.reason: The vulnerability root cause explicitly states that the function failed to validate CPU ownership before manipulating state, causing out-of-bounds access. Group 1 directly addresses this by adding a conditional check to confirm the CID is on CPU before performing the drop operation, which mitigates the identified security flaw.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement manipulates the CID mask without first validating that the CID is actually CPU-owned. When the TRANSIT flag is set, the CID may appear CPU-owned but is actually in transit, causing out-of-bounds access when clear_bit() operates on an invalid mm_cidmask reference. The function mm_drop_cid_on_cpu() fails to check the TRANSIT flag before performing this state manipulation.
